title: Unified admin change gating and routing playbook for RBAC / SSO / SCIM requests
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a single structured intake and prioritization playbook to route admin-related customer requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning issues, org policy exceptions) to the correct owner and SLA tier. Goal: reduce time-to-resolution for enterprise admin changes, cut manual triage work by CSMs, and ensure sensitive changes get proper compliance review before granting elevated access.
background: We currently have multiple ad-hoc intake channels (support tickets, sales ask, account exec emails) and inconsistent triage heuristics. This increases lead time for enterprise customers requesting RBAC templates, SSO onboarding, SCIM sync troubleshooting, or org-level policy exceptions. Teams involved: Support, Solutions Engineering, Security & Compliance, Identity, Platform. This playbook will define structured intake fields, an automated scoring router, manual escalation paths, SLAs, and audit hooks.
scope: Intake form schema for all admin access requests, scoring model and routing rules to map to owner queues (Support Level 2, Solutions Eng, Identity Eng, Security Review), SLAs by priority, user-facing acknowledgement templates, audit/logging requirements, and rollout plan for Console + email intake. Does NOT include changes to RBAC enforcement code or new identity protocol implementations.
acceptance_criteria: A single intake form available in Console and support portal capturing standardized fields (customer org, requester role, change type, urgency, justification, affected resources, audit approval docs)
Automated scoring returns a routing decision and SLA tier for 95% of incoming requests during pilot
Playbook includes clear human escalation paths for security-sensitive changes with a 48-hour max review window
Acknowledgement + status updates sent to requester within 1 hour of submission
Audit trail created for all granted org-level changes with links to approval artifacts and PR/Runbook references
Pilot run with three enterprise customers and reduction in mean time to resolution (MTTR) by at least 30% vs current baseline
intake_form_fields: attachments: config_screenshots, logs, SAML metadata, audit_records
scoring_rubric: Automated flags: requests modifying owner/admin roles OR touching billing/org-settings => auto-high-priority and require security review
SSO onboarding: if IdP metadata missing or certificate expired => route to Identity Eng with P1 SLA
SCIM sync: if >100k users affected or provisioning errors >0.5% failure rate => escalate to Solutions Eng and Platform
Low-risk role assignments (non-owner, non-billing) => support L2 can approve within SLA after verification
Customer tier: Enterprise customers may get expedited routing if committed in contract
routing_targets: Customer Success (communication and follow-through for contract-mandated SLAs)
sla_matrix: P0/high-risk/security: initial response 1 hour, security review start within 4 hours, final decision 48 hours
P1/SSO-blocking or major onboarding: initial response 2 hours, engineering engagement within 12 hours, resolution target 5 business days
P2/minor RBAC changes: response within 8 hours, resolution target 3 business days
P3/documentation or non-blocking requests: response within 72 hours
pilot_plan: Week 0: finalize intake schema and implement Console form + support-portal webhook
Week 1-2: enable automated scorer and route to internal queues; dry-run with internal test orgs
Week 3-6: run pilot with 3 enterprise customers (1 fintech, 1 healthcare, 1 SaaS) and collect MTTR, accuracy of routing, false-positive security flags
Week 7: iterate on scoring thresholds and playbook text based on pilot feedback
Week 8: rollout to all enterprise customers with monitoring and rollback plan
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager automatic approvals could grant elevated access incorrectly => Mitigation: default to require manual approval for owner/billing changes and add audit blockers
Risk: Increased load on Identity Eng during rollout => Mitigation: temporary staffing buffer + documented onboarding checklist to reduce edge-case triage time
Risk: Customer frustration if SLAs not met => Mitigation: clear acknowledgement + status page for each request and CSM notifications for high-impact customers
